guardianfootball.description: Latest team news, Premier League buildup and more Get in touch: email the matchday live team Crack open the Vitamin D supplements, there doesn’t seem to be much sign of sunshine anywhere across the UK today. Certainly the sky in Lincoln looks very similar to the one outside my window in London. Wesley Fofana was booed by Chelsea’s fans yesterday, and substituted early in the second half, after his decision to give an unauthorised interview to a French YouTuber, in which he joked about the club’s Carabao Cup defeat to Liverpool, and for which he has apologised and which he has promised not to repeat. Among other things, supporters sang “You’re not welcome here” when he was on the ball. This…

guardianfootball.title: Basque to the future: Andoni Iraola fired up for first Merseyside derby
guardianfootball.description: Liverpool head coach sees parallels with Athletic v Sociedad derby as he comes up against his old foe David Moyes “I haven’t lived this derby,” Andoni Iraola acknowledged, and yet he already feels it. A former Athletic Bilbao captain coming up against an ex-Real Sociedad head coach needs no instruction on the importance of winning a derby, whether in the Basque country or on Merseyside. But this week, as the Liverpool head coach approaches his first experience of the latter, there has been no escape. “It has been very easy for me here,” says Iraola of his five months on Merseyside. “Family-wise we have settled in really well. People here are very friendly, they love to talk to you but in a…

guardianfootball.title: Gibbs-White and Igor Jesus fire Nottingham Forest past shaky Chelsea
guardianfootball.description: Wesley Fofana, as a former Leicester player, might have expected the celebrating Nottingham Forest fans to give him a hard time. But, at the end of a week in which he invited opprobrium by making light of missing a penalty at Liverpool in an unsanctioned French interview, he endured the ultimate ignominy when Chelsea supporters followed a four-letter suggestion to tell the defender: “You’re not welcome here.” Fofana was humiliated by Liam Delap before fouling the former Chelsea striker for a penalty that Morgan Gibbs-White converted for the first of his two goals. The result, coming after Forest’s win against Manchester City in their last match at the City Ground, means they climb three…

guardianfootball.title: Spygate tensions erupt at Southampton after Finn Azaz’s cry-baby celebration riles Boro
guardianfootball.description: When asked whether he had any regrets about running the length of the pitch to goad the Middlesbrough supporters he used to call his own with a mock crying celebration, Finn Azaz was unequivocal. “None whatsoever,” said the Southampton playmaker. And you get the sense that very few associated with his club disagreed. Southampton, and their manager Tonda Eckert, long ago admitted their Spygate crime. Based on the behaviour of many connected to the south-coast club – their manager a notable exception – they have embraced it. The sense of aggrievement that it cost them the chance of promotion last season remains. Continue reading...

guardianfootball.title: The Renéessance is over but Arsenal’s chaotic cycle will go on without further change | Suzanne Wrack
guardianfootball.description: Renée Slegers’ exit, 18 months on from European glory, was inevitable but much of the blame lies with those higher up The Renéessance is over. Three down, how many more to go? The exit of Arsenal manager, Renée Slegers, 18 months after delivering European glory was somewhat inevitable, her position made untenable after six home draws in six games and just 15 points from 11 games, but will it solve the Gunners’ problems? There were high expectations in north London prior to the season, after difficult starts in back-to-back WSL campaigns put them outside a real title challenge within the opening few games. Continue reading...

guardianfootball.title: Arteta sets Arsenal 100-point Premier League target to emulate Manchester City
guardianfootball.description: ‘It’s only been done once and that’s what we want’ Arteta not being drawn on City’s financial charges Mikel Arteta has set Arsenal the ­target of emulating Manchester City by becoming only the second team in Premier League history to record 100 points in a season. Arteta was an assistant for Pep Guardiola’s side when they achieved the landmark in the 2017-18 campaign, beating second-placed Manchester United by 19 points. City head to the Emirates Stadium on Sunday already trailing Arsenal by six points after just 11 games, with Enzo Maresca’s side having failed to win any of their four previous league matches. Continue reading...

guardianfootball.title: ‘My Tottenham was born’: De Zerbi harks back to opening defeat for Sunderland return
guardianfootball.description: Spurs head coach intends to draw on last season’s trauma Italian praises club after Williams-Barnett signs contract Tottenham’s trip to Sunderland takes Roberto De Zerbi back to the start. The Italian’s first game as the club’s manager came at the Stadium of Light in April and relegation was on the cards when his new side slipped to a 1-0 defeat . The result left Spurs in the bottom three, two points below West Ham, and De Zerbi has not forgotten the reaction in the dressing room after the final whistle. Survival was secured on the final day of last season but he is taking nothing for granted after a promising run of form. Continue reading...

guardianfootball.title: Columbus Crew eliminate Messi and Inter Miami from MLS playoffs with stoppage-time strike
guardianfootball.description: Santiago Rodríguez strikes in stoppage time to seal win Inter Miami fail to defend 2025 MLS Cup title. Messi retired internationally earlier this year Inter Miami’s quest to defend their MLS Cup title is over. The South Florida side had two gilt-edged chances to take the lead in Game 2 of their best-of-three first-round series against Columbus in the MLS Playoffs on Friday, but missed both of them along with several others, later succumbing to a terrific stoppage-time winner from Santi Rodríguez in a 1-0 win for the Crew. Continue reading...

pitchfork.description: The third in a series dedicated to the Spanish pop vanguard of the 1980s captures a moment when Franco’s dictatorship gave way to an explosion of youthful creativity across post-punk, new wave, and more.

pitchfork.description: On her first release under her own name, Liz Harris immerses us in the the ambient side of Grouper with two long-form instrumental compositions.

pitchfork.description: Colombia’s TraTraTrax label gathers unreleased tracks from a shadowy internet collective that’s been making mischief on the fringes of the Brazilian funk scene for more than two decades.

pitchfork.description: The Texas singer-songwriter’s debut channels a cool-girl-next-door vibe and a twangy alt-pop sound. At her best, she sounds wise beyond her years, with a knack for hooks and a literary imagination.

pitchfork.title: American Bully XL
pitchfork.description: On its second album, the Texas quartet runs classic country influences through blasts of distortion, pairing its noisy palette with newly confessional lyrics.

pitchfork.title: Thanatos
pitchfork.description: Bradford Cox’s first solo album in 15 years is a haunted, autumnal meditation on all forms of decay: bodily, spiritual, political, and sonic.

pitchfork.title: Demoed EP
pitchfork.description: MJ Lenderman, Circuit des Yeux, Flock of Dimes, and more lend their voices to stripped-down versions of songs from this year’s Punching the Clown on a new EP that continues the remarkable transformation of Lambchop.

pitchfork.title: Khudgarzi
pitchfork.description: The singer-songwriter tells stories of strange and solitary women cast out by society: murderers, sex workers, and schemers determined to secure their freedom by any means.

quietus.title: Remembering Jean-Claude Vannier
quietus.description: Serge Gainsbourg biographer Jeremy Allen looks back at the life and times of an inspired French composer. Main portrait by Léo Alestro, with thanks to Ipecac I was lucky enough to meet Jean-Claude Vannier, the French composer who died on Friday 27 November aged 83, on two separate occasions. The first time was at his apartment in the 3eme arrondissement of Paris, which was reached via the creakiest of paternoster lifts before entering into what was, by Parisian standards, a spacious room. Among its contents, everything seemed secondary to the white grand piano. It was 2011 and I was interviewing the preternaturally gifted musician and arranger for The Stool Pigeon, and while that’s 15…

quietus.title: Paperback Writers: Why Do Rock Stars Make Terrible Novelists?
quietus.description: The Go-Betweens' Robert Forster has a novel out – it joins a wretched parade of books by pop musicians hellbent on parlaying their fame in the publishing world Earlier this year, Robert Forster, ex-Go-Between and respected elder-statesman of indie rock, did something only a handful of his peers have had the nerve – or foolhardiness – to do before. He put his reputation on the line, flung all caution to the wind and went and published a novel. In doing so he joined a coterie of A-listers who, at some point in their careers, decided to apply their considerable talents as songwriters to longform prose fiction: a not-too-shabby crew that includes the likes of Bob Dylan, Gil Scott-Heron, Robert…

quietus.title: Jean-Claude Vannier has Died, Aged 83
quietus.description: The French composer was famed for his work on Serge Gainsbourg's Histoire de Melody Nelson Jean-Claude Vannier, the widely respected French composer and arranger whose work lit up Serge Gainsbourg's 1971 concept album Histoire de Melody Nelson, has died at the age of 83. He passed away in Paris earlier today (27 November), Libération reports. "Jean-Claude Vannier was a singular, unclassifiable, profoundly independent artist whose creativity and audacity transcended generations ," said Virginie Vannier, one of his daughters, in a message sent to AFP. Vannier's daughter's tribute continued: "His work has inspired international artists such as Beck and Mike Patton, and his compositions have…

quietus.title: Outer Waves Announces First Acts Playing 2027 Edition
quietus.description: Merzbow, The Ex and more will play the Liverpool event next May The Ex, photo by Maarten Mooijman Outer Waves has shared the first wave of acts playing its 2027 edition. The festival returns to Liverpool for its third edition next May, and will take over the venues Invisible Wind Factory, Make. and Quarry. The lineup will be headed up by Merzbow and The Ex. Also confirmed to play are Nihiloxica, Sex Swing, Poor Creature, Palestinian Sound Archive, Penelope Trappes, Ancient Grains, Those Holy, Cowtown, The Aleph and All Maudra. More names will be added to the bill in the coming months. Outer Waves will take place from 15 to 16 May 2027. Find more information here. ...

quietus.title: The Strange World Of… H.P. Lovecraft Film Adaptations
quietus.description: Mat Colegate uses an unutterable, indescribable, cosmically horrific dialectic to suss out why so many great films have come out of such problematic source material How to solve a problem like Howard Phillips Lovecraft? As an author he is maybe second only to Tolkien in the extraordinary reach of his influence on pop culture, with a legacy that encompasses literary prizes, beanie toys and band names, not to mention a reputation as one of the foundational architects of the weird fiction genre. He was a tormented but highly imaginative writer whose best work often displays a prophetic edge; he was the cultural figure aside from Shakespeare with the most recognisable silhouette; and, as even…

quietus.title: Music of the Month: The Best Albums and Tracks of November 2026
quietus.description: tQ's staffers round up everything that's excellent from the last few weeks in music Although End Of Year list season is very nearly upon us, November has been such a sterling month for new music that we couldn't resist one more of our monthly round-ups. Below you'll find everything we've loved, from riotous Brazilian funk to avant-garde space trumpet. Everything featured below, as well as all the other knockout music we’ve covered at tQ this month, will be compiled into an hours-long playlist exclusive to our subscribers. In addition, subscribers can enjoy exclusive music from some of the world’s most forward-thinking artists, regular deep-dive essays, a monthly podcast, specially-curated…

quietus.title: Laura Cannell – Winter Rites
quietus.description: Laura Cannell Winter Rites Recorded at the Octagon Unitarian Chapel in Norwich, the English composer and improviser welcomes in the season of Advent WINTER RITES by Laura Cannell Although we do not often think to question it, the church organ is a strange concept. Uniquely, it is tied to its location, more like a building than an instrument. While the organ triggers sound, the resonance of its building is what shapes it. The acoustics of every church or chapel are different, and every organ is therefore a unique instrument with a signature sound generated belonging to just one place. The place specificity of the church organ, and its responsiveness to conditions, was recently explored by…

quietus.title: Main’s ‘Motion Pool’ Set for Vinyl Reissue
quietus.description: The duo's 1994 debut album has been remastered and will be newly released with three extra tracks Photo by Tom Sheehan Main's 1994 debut album Motion Pool is being reissued. The record, which followed an initial series of EPs from Robert Hampson and Scott Dowson's project, has been remastered for the updated edition, which will also take in three additional tracks from the era of the original album's production. It will be a double-vinyl release. Blending Hampson and Dowson's history with post-rock and drone music as part of Loop, Motion Pool saw the duo push their sound further into the ambient and abstract territory that they sought to explore more deeply together as Main. Speaking about…

aquariumdrunkard.title: Erasmo Carlos :: Carlos, Erasmo (1971)
aquariumdrunkard.description: At once freezing and tropical, airy and baroque, swinging with dizzying freedom between electric and acoustic, fuzzed-out and bare, wound-up and laid-back. It’s a little chimera of garage-soul MPB: it bites, it grooves, it drives, it eventually rests. Now reissued by Vampisoul less than a decade after Light in the Attic’s historic 2017 reedition, it arrives like a second knock on a door that, half a century later, is still only ajar.

aquariumdrunkard.title: David Axelrod :: S/T
aquariumdrunkard.description: In 2000, cinematic composer and jazz producer David Axelrod was invited to record a new album by British label Mo' Wax (DJ Shadow, Parsley Sound). The self-titled record was built upon the discovery of rare acetates that were to be the final installment of Axelrod's shapeshifting sixties trilogy with the Electric Prunes such as the Latin-sung, psychedelic Mass in F Minor. This eponymous record is starkly referential to all of the various stages of Axelrod's iconoclast career, from his catalogue becoming an endless sample trove for hip-hop architects to reconnecting with sixties collaborators like soul singer Lou Rawls.

aquariumdrunkard.title: Spike Fuck :: Evidence
aquariumdrunkard.description: Spike Fuck lives in restless extremity. The Australian art punk provocateur has tried all the vices—heroin, cigarettes, religion, abstinence—one by one. For a period in the teens, he transitioned medically, recording and performing as a woman, before changing back again in the 2020s. He lived in a monastery at one point. None of these experiments gave him what he was looking for, so he discarded them just as easily as he picked them up.

aquariumdrunkard.title: The Aquarium Drunkard Show: SIRIUS/XMU (7pm PST, Channel 35)
aquariumdrunkard.description: Outré California. Broadcasting from northeast Los Angeles — the Aquarium Drunkard Show on SIRIUS/XMU, channel 35. 7pm California time, Wednesdays. Post-punk, synth weirdness, crooked outsider pop, shadowy electronics, dubby rhythms, warped grooves. 34.1090° N, 118.2334° W

aquariumdrunkard.title: Late November :: Autumnal Britfolk Instrumentals (1968-1981)
aquariumdrunkard.description: The shadows are lengthening, the leaves are falling, the air is getting crisp. That’s right, we’re heading into the latter days of autumn. Maybe the best time of year? One of them, anyway. The season demands a soundtrack, and for some reason, the loosely organized britfolk genre is perfect for these days. So here’s an hour’s worth of instrumentals from the late 1960s to the early 1980s, when giants walked the earth. Trad melodies and rhythms abound, but there are plenty of left-turns, mostly thanks to dedicated iconoclasts like John Martyn, Davey Graham and Michael Chapman. Grab a pint of something dark and rich and settle in.

aquariumdrunkard.title: Transmissions :: Beth Orton
aquariumdrunkard.description: This week on the show, we’re presenting the penultimate episode of our 12th season. And we’ve saved a tremendous talk for this second to last installment: our guest is singer/songwriter Beth Orton. In the mid-’90s, she emerged as a purveyor of electronic folk, working with artists like William Orbit, The Chemical Brothers, and Four Tet. Her latest is The Ground Above. Reviewing it for Aquarium Drunkard, Kyle Lemmon described it as “a free-flowing mixture of electronic funk, spirit walking jazz, and ambient folk.”

aquariumdrunkard.title: The Lagniappe Sessions :: Shane Butler
aquariumdrunkard.description: Shane Butler's first solo record, Heavy Debt , is due next month, and for this Lagniappe Session he's pulled together three songs that have been rattling around for a long time. Fugazi's "I'm So Tired," a song he first encountered as a kid watching skate videos, Shoes' homemade pop and a 1979 Soft Boys' nugget.

aquariumdrunkard.title: Miles Davis: Copenhagen Live 1969
aquariumdrunkard.description: Miles Davis’ 1969 live ensemble existed in a parallel timeline alongside his studio work - greasing his audience for a future for which they were wholly unprepared. A new 2LP set, Copenhagen Live 1969 , captures the band at its peak, stress-testing then-unreleased Bitches Brew material, tearing it down and reassembling it into some of the most far-out, formless music of Miles’ career.

mubi.title: A Sharing of Souls: Ryûsuke Hamaguchi Discusses “All of a Sudden”

At 197 minutes, Ryûsuke Hamaguchi’s latest film, All of a Sudden (2026), is neither the longest nor the most radical of the Japanese director’s dozen-plus features. In fact, its story, about two women of different cultural backgrounds who meet and grow close over the course of a few weeks, is decidedly straightforward and occasionally even sentimental—a far cry from the convoluted, miserabilist narratives that tend to dominate the world of international art cinema. Inspired by When Life Suddenly Takes a Turn: Twenty Letters Between a Philosopher with Terminal Cancer and a Medical Anthropologist , a collection of epistolary nonfiction written by…

mubi.title: A World in Parts
mubi.description: The Journey (Peter Watkins, 1987). At Radio Canada, preparations are underway for Ronald Reagan’s 1985 summit with Canadian prime minister Brian Mulroney. Filmmaker Peter Watkins and his crew have been allowed into meetings where the broadcasters plan their coverage down to the second. Everyone must synchronize their watches: A discrepancy of 40 seconds, one participant warns, could throw off the day’s work. A shot requested at 17:02 might be missed if recorded 30 seconds later. “One thing is certain: there can’t be anything unexpected tonight,” another member of the team declares. Security officials will provide the presidential route, street by street, allowing the text to be prepared…
